service.description:
The shell counts of a user: the service named by STRT_SHELL_COUNTS_SERVICE in the user's theme for STT_INTERNAL_QUASAR (found as a render finds it: the user's, a group's, the type's enumCode, a DEFAULT theme of the type; DEFAULT_QUASAR when there is none) is called with userId and its counts map returned. counts is null when the theme has no such value, and when the service is missing, fails or answers no map, which is logged once per service name. Another user's counts only with authorization disabled (internal work).
The counts service takes userId and answers counts, a map the shell reads by key: today, chat, email (external mail unread), messages (internal messages and the mailbox posts delivered to the Inbox), notifications (unviewed in the NinNotifications inbox and approvals waiting), approvals and updates (unviewed in NinUpdates, which no header badge shows), each a number or a map with a total; the framework sends it as it is.

Send each user their shell counts (get#ShellCounts) as a NotificationMessage on the topic shellCounts: not persisted, showAlert false, the counts as its message. Coalesced per user: at most one send every 2 seconds, and the requests inside that window fold into one send at its end. Inside a transaction the request waits for the commit (a rollback sends nothing), and the sends are made on a thread of the server, so the caller never waits for the counts. The EECAs and SECAs on the records the counts read call this.

parameter.name: userIdList
parameter.description: A list of userId, or a comma separated text

service.description: The contract of a quick-create kind's condition-service (xml-screen-3.xsd quick-create): whether to offer the kind to the session's user. The shell calls it as the app root that declares the kind, in a transaction of its own, each time it makes the shell data; offer true offers it, false or no answer leaves it out, and one that fails is logged and leaves out that kind alone. It answers about the session's user only.

The providers of hook declared in the shell-providers of the app roots the current user may open, in sequence order: sourceId (the provider's name), app and service. A screen offers a feature that needs a provider (the Internal account, filing on a record) only when there is one.

Call each provider of hook declared by the app roots the current user may open, or only the one named sourceId, with parameters, as the app that declares it (its screen is the artifact the call runs under, so its authorization and entity filters apply; a userId or app passed in parameters grants nothing). A read (the default) runs each provider in its own transaction: one that fails is logged by name and listed in failedParts ({sourceId, error}) and the others still answer. A mutation (record-link, create-from, invitation) runs in the caller's transaction and stops at the first failure, which is an error. results holds each provider's answer with its sourceId, in order; each source pages itself, and pages are never joined into one. unavailable is true when no app the user may open declares the hook, which is not the same as providers that answer nothing.

The appearance of a Quasar theme for the current user, as the shell gets it in config.appearance: colorSchemes (each id, description, light, dark, custom, version and the fonts it uses when the user has chosen none), fonts, defaultSchemeId (STRT_DEFAULT_COLOR_SCHEME, when it is a scheme of the theme), schemeId (the user's scheme, else the default), policy (STRT_APPEARANCE_POLICY: appearance, mode, a flag per group, lockedKeys), values (the user's THEME_* preferences the policy allows), keys (each appearance preference and its group), tokens (brand, surface, shape) and links (the style sheets of the scheme and fonts the page links).
Each STRT_APPEARANCE_SERVICE of the theme is called in sequence with userId, screenThemeId and the appearance so far, and answers appearance, which the next one gets: it may add or remove schemes and fonts, set the default scheme or tighten and loosen the policy. One that fails or answers no map is logged and skipped. The locked values, the effective scheme and the links are worked out after the last one, and setPreference refuses a locked key with the same policy.

parameter.name: screenThemeId
parameter.description: Default the current user's theme of type STT_INTERNAL_QUASAR

service.description: The appearance policy of the current user's Quasar theme, after its STRT_APPEARANCE_SERVICE services (what get#Appearance answers as policy), as JSON text: appearance, mode, a flag per group (mode, density, scheme, accent, colors, fonts, sizes, motion) and lockedKeys. For a component's own appearance form; ec.user.setPreference refuses what it locks either way.

The current user's Quasar theme (screen theme type STT_INTERNAL_QUASAR): one of the themes that get#Appearance offers for the user's current theme, after its STRT_APPEARANCE_SERVICE services. Refused, with nothing written, for another theme or when the current theme's policy locks the choice (theme false, or appearance false). Choosing the theme the user would get without a row of their own (a group's, the type's default) deletes their UserScreenTheme, so a later change of the group's theme reaches them; another theme is written. A change of theme clears the user's THEME_COLOR_SCHEME, so the new theme opens in its own default scheme; the other appearance choices are kept. The page reloads to show the new theme.

The style sheet of a color scheme: the brand colors as --q-* !important, the other tokens as --m-*, the dark panel and page also as --q-dark and --q-dark-page, the dark link giving way to the user's dark accent, then the scheme's extraCss. A name or value that could end its declaration is logged and left out; an unknown scheme is empty.
